# icom

**Minimal CI-V control for Icom radios from the command line**

- **Version recorded:** 20120228
- **Categories:** `rig-control`
- **Upstream:** <https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/icom>

## What it does

Sends CI-V commands to an Icom transceiver over a serial interface -- setting frequency and mode, reading back what the radio reports -- as a small standalone program with no library dependency.

## Why you would want it

Rarely, and deliberately so. Hamlib's `rigctl` covers this and far more. What this offers is directness: it speaks the CI-V protocol with nothing in between, which makes it useful for understanding the protocol or for debugging a case where hamlib's backend is itself suspect.

## Before it will work

An Icom radio with a CI-V interface, the correct CI-V address, and access to the serial device.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install icom --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `icom`

## Known problems

The version string is its release date and it is from 2012; the CI-V command set has grown since. It has no upstream Homepage in Debian and no project page to point at, so what the distribution ships is what exists. For ordinary rig control, use libhamlib-utils instead -- this is carried for the narrow case where the simpler tool is the more useful one.
